Just days after Grand Theft Auto 6’s massive November 19 launch, a PlayStation player has found themselves in hot water after sharing a NSFW image from the game with a PSN friend.

Player derickgott007 shared his experience on X (via TweakTown) that he received a 30-day ban from PlayStation’s social features after sharing a photo from GTA 6’s infamous nudist resort, leading him to put out a strong warning on social media.

Recent findings suggest that while the offending image was not shared, GTA 6’s nudist areas feature a mix of fully clothed and naked NPCs roaming around, mirroring the real experiences of clothing-optional resorts that are a roaring trade in coastal Florida. The image was sent via PSN’s private message service and not posted publicly on any part of Sony’s gaming service.

According to recent reports, although the photo was taken with GTA 6’s in-game camera application and did not feature real-world nudity, PlayStation somehow flagged the image as pornographic and sent a message saying it breached the service’s Code of Conduct. The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The game’s hyper-realistic graphics might have tricked Sony’s strict auto-moderation tools that real sensitive images were being sent.

The player was warned that any further infractions could lead to permanent suspension, causing him to frantically post on social media about his experience.

In their post, the player cautioned others: "Do not, I repeat, do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity." The official notice from PlayStation Safety confirmed the content "breached the Code of Conduct" and cited "pornographic or obscene content.".

The ban comes as a real risk for players who share content from the game online, meaning auto-moderation tools on social media or messaging services may inadvertently restrict content featuring risque or outright obscene imagery.

While PSN flagged pornographic content, the irony comes that Sony is actively promoting Grand Theft Auto 6 on a grand scale across its platform, featuring multiple ads and promotional images that encourage players to pick the game up on PlayStation.

However, Sony also has to abide with the local laws of the hundreds of countries it operates in, meaning that its auto-moderation tools must respond quickly to perceived threats or the breaking of rules to protect young and vulnerable customers from harm. The company does not grant exceptions, even for unedited screenshots captured from M-rated games sold directly through its own storefront.

Sony also has to abide with the local laws of the hundreds of countries it operates in, meaning that its auto-moderation tools must respond swiftly to perceived threats.

In a recent development, the response has been mixed, with netizens online commenting that the ban is disproportionately harsh considering the image came from a game being actively pushed by Sony. Others argued that rules are rules, and that perhaps instead of a ban, Sony should simply block the offending content to prevent it being seen by the receiving party.

One user even urged derickgott07 to sue Sony in a class action lawsuit, saying the firm “wouldn’t have a leg to stand on” and that it broke its own Code of Conduct by selling a sexually explicit game on its own marketplace. Figure that one out.

The line-up of ExpMoe, calamity, vanitas, yearn and dynamic was one of eight teams Riot Games invited directly to the North America Qualifier Playoffs. Cloud9, ENVY and two Shopify Rebellion line-ups were also on that list.

Recent findings suggest that before facing Maryville, QoR edged Shopify Rebellion Gold 2-1 in round two. In the Swiss stage, two wins sent a team through and two losses knocked it out. QoR sit 99th in the Elo power rankings, with a rating of 1590 and a 37-34 record across 71 rated matches.

Maryville came through the second open qualifier, held from 12 to 15 November, which drew 512 teams. They finished in the top two of that bracket. They then opened this event by sweeping Shopify Rebellion Gold.

It has been revealed that A 0-2 loss to Cloud9 followed, and defeat by QoR left them with two losses. In the other round-three matches, Oafs beat SaD Esports, counterfeit beat FlyQuest and Wildcard beat Winthrop, each without dropping a map. The Elo table places Maryville 161st, with a rating of 1521 and a 6-7 record in 13 rated matches.

In a recent development, the playoffs are an eight-team double-elimination bracket. The winner takes North America’s direct place at the 2027 VCT Americas Kickoff in São Paulo. The runner-up goes to the Americas Last Chance Qualifier, also in São Paulo, on 17 and 18 December. That event is the last route into Kickoff. Eight partner teams are invited to Kickoff, and four places go to non-partner teams.

Riot runs the North America qualifiers with Red Bull. They also serve as the North America qualifiers for Red Bull Home Ground. The Los Angeles event runs from 10 to 13 December. Ten teams will play for a total prize pool of $100,000 USD. Eight are invited from around the world, and two earn their places through regional qualifiers. Riot will also reveal the 2027 Kickoff draws live on stage there.

Recent findings suggest that fnatic are EMEA’s invited team. The organisation is rebuilding its roster after parting with several players, including long-serving captain Jake ‘Boaster’ Howlett, Red Bull stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in Grand Theft Auto 6, Jason and Lucia will have three main stats to track: Health, Stamina, and Focus. All three stats can be monitored using the Fitness app on their phones and boosted by completing specific tasks.

It has been revealed that health, in particular, is the stat that determines how much damage you can take before you get the dreaded Wasted screen. Increasing this stat can make fights easier and also prevent you from being killed if you hit something while flying down the highways of Leonida. For that reason, it's probably the most vital stat to train, and you'll need to do it consistently.

Sources indicate that like the other two stats, Health maxes out at Level 4, and the main way to increase it is by working out. Certain workouts can also increase Stamina, so you want to focus on Strength workouts for Health. Additionally, you can only do up to three workouts per day, so you won't be able to spend a whole in-game day at the gym to knock this out a level in one go.

Jason and Lucia's stats are independent of each other. Working out one character does not raise the overall stats for both; you will need to put in time for both to raise their individual stats.

As for the strength workouts themselves, you'll need to keep increasing the weight limit to improve your Health as each character becomes stronger. Additionally, pay attention to the workout window on your Fitness App. If too much time passes between workouts, and you neglect them, you'll start to see a negative impact on your Health instead.

The strength workouts you can do include:.

Gyms aren't the only places you can find the equipment for these workouts either. There are various workout spots throughout the game, including the house in Key Lento and beaches.

According to recent reports, don't start a workout with low Stamina. If you don't have enough Stamina, you will fail the workout because you can't finish the set.

Sources indicate that in addition to the workouts, you also need to monitor your hunger and sleep. Allowing either of these to fall too low will ultimately hurt your progress and recovery time, so be sure to check these stats in the Fitness app before working out and complete them immediately after the workout if needed.

As long as you're sticking to your workouts and taking care of yourself, you should be able to maintain both Jason and Lucia's max Health benefits with ease.

  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Upgrade, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Sources indicate that since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Patch to actually see it in action.

It has been revealed that the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

It has been revealed that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside newly introduced Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

Industry observers note that we've been keeping an eye out for news of Nintendo's playable and electric ocarinas going on sale in Europe for a good while now. It looks like sales are just around the corner, but you're going to need to jump through some hoops if you want to get your hands on one.

Both the Nintendo playable model and HORI electric version will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. You can register your interest in getting either model now on the Nintendo website, but there are some criteria that you'll have to pass first.

It has been revealed that firstly, you'll need to have a Nintendo account registered in Europe (excluding Norway, Russia and South Africa), have allowed Nintendo to process your usage information to customise services, offers and recommendations in your Nintendo Account settings, and have allowed Nintendo to send email recommendations about games, events, special offers and more. You'll need to have done all of that by 22nd November.

You can only register your interest if you have "reached at least 10 hours of play time in the Nintendo Switch 2 game The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time by 18/11/2026" using the same Nintendo account you use to register.

Industry observers note that and that's just to get an invite. On the day that the products become available, those who are invited will receive an email with a link to purchase either ocarina (limited to one each per customer).

According to recent reports, the playable ocarina will set you back £29.99, bundling the instrument with a wrist strap and sheet music for all of the in-game songs. HORI's electric option is a little more expensive at £41.99, but also comes with a dedicated stand.

Have you registered your interest for either model? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next substantial game has officially debuted.
  • The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.
  • Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next substantial game has officially debuted. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

According to recent reports, the open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

It has been revealed that in Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially rolled out, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

It has been revealed that numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Sources indicate that indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

It has been revealed that the mod, known as OcarinaVR, was developed by ReTracedGames and builds upon the previously released PC port. It is showing the true skills of the PC modding community, and at what speed they can work to develop player experiences beyond a game’s original console boundaries.

The power of the OcarinaVR mod is quite the sight to behold. It goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective with accurate spatial scaling—meaning the world adjusts depending on whether the player is controlling young Link or the grown-up version.

The mod also brings intricate control mechanics and hand tracking, allowing players to map and control Link’s arms and individual fingers using their VR controllers. Swinging the Master sword and bashing enemies with the Hylian shield never looks so satisfying and adds a sense of depth and realism to the game beyond just its graphics.

Recent findings suggest that ocarinaVR also manages UI elements and prevents clutter, displaying HUD readouts like heart count and the minimap as floating panels. Pre-rendered cutscenes are displayed on a curved virtual cinema screen for maximum immersion as the perspective shifts back to the 3rd person.

OcarinaVR … goes beyond just being a camera trick, and instead shifts the entire game into a true first-person perspective.

According to recent reports, the mod is based on the Hookshot PC recompilation that was released on PC shortly after Ocarina of Time released on Nintendo Switch 2 on November 5. That release already brought native widescreen and uncapped framerates, meaning it was a solid foundation for the OcarinaVR mod to build off.

Sources indicate that fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental, with players praising its highly-detailed graphics and faithful retelling of the classic Zelda tale. Critics loved it equally as much, giving it one of the highest ratings on Metacritic of all time—a solid 95/100 aggregated score.

In DualShockers’ own review, Tayna Garcia wrote that the remake gives returning players an “opportunity to experience those same feelings again” from their childhoods, powered by nostalgia, but mentioned it's a perfect place for newcomers to start their Zelda journey, too.

Fan response to the Ocarina of Time remake has been monumental [and] critics loved it equally as much.

In a recent development, the game was swiftly followed by Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6—perhaps the most hyped game of all time (and the highest reviewed on Metacritic with a stunning score of 99). Nintendo knew to get Zelda out the door before the news cycle and social media turned to GTA 6 for who knows how long.

The new VR mod gives fans a chance to take on Ocarina of Time in a whole new way, snatching a little bit of attention back from the Vice City-drenched mediascape right now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There hasn't been a new mainline Banjo-Kazooie game for almost 20 years, which is just wild when you really stop and think about it. Despite glimmers of hope here and there, there has been no revival, but now fans of the series might have been thrown their most hopeful rope yet, as Activision Blizzard seemingly views the dormant IP as one of the most important under its newly expanded gaze.

In a newly introduced job listing for an Activision product manager that would handle and help promote emerging franchises, Banjo-Kazooie is one of a handful of major franchises that now reside under the Xbox-owned studio. "Activision is home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now... Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo-Kazooie," the job description reads.

In a recent development, certain studios now answering to Activision were among many significant changes rolled out during Xbox's most recent round of layoffs. The next Halo will be an Activision game, and World's Edge and Rare are both under Activision now too, which is why Age of Empires and Sea of Thieves are mentioned in the job listing.

Banjo-Kazooie may well be Rare's best-loved and most famous export, so it makes sense that Activision would want to brag about now having it under its umbrella. Mentioning it in a job listing in this way, though, has renewed hope that we're finally getting a upcoming Banjo game. Not just because every other series mentioned is active in one way or another, but because it's mentioned in a job listing for someone who will be responsible for emerging franchises.

When Xbox revealed that Activision will be in charge of Halo's future, fans of the series were left feeling a little uncertain. Banjo fans might now be feeling the same way, although they probably shouldn't be. As Activision highlights, it also owns Crash and Spyro, two colorful platformers who are often lumped together with Banjo when people list the best and most famous games and characters from that genre, and the little purple dragon is getting his first new game since 2004 next year - Spyro: A Realm Beyond.

According to recent reports, both Spyro and Crash have enjoyed huge success via their remastered trilogies too, both selling in the millions. Perhaps that will be Activision's first order of business with Banjo now that it is directly working with Rare. A remastered trilogy that introduces the original game, Banjo-Tooie, and Nuts & Bolts to a whole upcoming generation of potential fans.

Industry observers note that it is just the name of the series listed alongside some other games for now, and we have kind of been here before. There have been rumblings that Banjo-Kazooie might be getting revived for years, only for those rumblings to repeatedly come to nothing. However, this is the biggest change the series has experienced in terms of who exactly is calling the shots when it comes to making a new Banjo game, and it's a studio that has more experience with platformers cut from the same cloth as Banjo than just about any other studio on the planet.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

Sources indicate that the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

It has been revealed that speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most key is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Sources indicate that going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Industry observers note that speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis stated this will work with latest and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

According to recent reports, pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in fresh saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

Sources indicate that you may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Recent findings suggest that lower down the list of urgent fixes is an upgrade that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Recent findings suggest that catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently confirmed that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.
  • It has been revealed that "We will continue to cherish what makes Persona unique, while also embracing changes in the times and needs, and taking on upcoming challenges.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there's been a lot of talk around how long GTA fans have been waiting for the latest entry to launch, but Persona isn't actually that far behind. Persona 5 – in its original state – released over a decade ago on 15th September 2016, and although Persona 6 has now been officially announced, we're none the wiser as to when it will actually come out.

It's likely to finally land at some point in 2027 after the dust has settled from Persona 4 Revival, but according to a recent interview with general producer Kazuhisa Wada (thanks, Nintendo Everything), fans won't have to wait quite so long for the inevitable Persona 7.

It has been revealed that "We will continue to cherish what makes Persona unique, while also embracing changes in the times and needs, and taking on upcoming challenges. We aim to be a brand that can grow for 5, 10 years, and beyond.

In a recent development, "Among those projects, the one we’re at the moment working on is Persona 6. While there’s still limited information I can share, we want to prove the results of all the challenges we’ve faced so far through the game itself. With that in mind, we’re creating something even better than before, and we’re feeling a real sense of accomplishment as we work on it.

"And Persona 6 is not the end. We are working on various things to ensure that you don’t have to wait as long for the next installment as we have in the past. And in order to make Persona an even bigger IP, we are constantly thinking about creative ideas and developments that will not disappoint your expectations. Please look forward to what’s to come from Persona.”.

We will look forward to it, Wada-san, thank you sir. Let's keep the focus on Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 for now though, hm?

It has been revealed that it's not a surprising statement, mind you. Game development is taking longer than ever these days, which also makes it more expensive than ever. So a lot of publishers are looking into potential solutions to cut down on dev time and increase the cadence of releases. As long as it doesn't involve handing everything off to AI, we're fine with that.

Persona 4 Revival is currently scheduled to launch on Switch 2 on 20th May 2027, a few months after other platforms. As for Persona 6, an imminent reveal has been rumoured recently thanks to a backend update on the official website. Hardly concrete, but it's a start.

What are your thoughts on Wada-san's comments here? Are you keen for the wait between mainline entries to be slightly shorter in the future? Let us know with a comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly posted Activision job listing has revealed that the mega-publisher might be planning to revive one of gaming’s most iconic character duos in a substantial way, after listing it alongside its other major active franchises like Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot and Halo.

It has been revealed that the organization name-dropped Banjo-Kazooie (thanks, Reddit) in the post beside its hugely successful IPs—an inclusion which came as a surprise to fans, considering the Rare property has been long dormant. It immediately ignited speculation online that Activision could be preparing a newly introduced major outing for the much-loved pair after years of collecting dust in the company’s trough of original characters.

In a recent development, out of all the franchises listed in the post’s mission statement, Banjo-Kazooie is the only one without an active game or modern entry, making its inclusion stick out like a sore thumb. Titles mentioned like Halo, Age of Empires and Sea of Thieves are all receiving major live-service support or have confirmed active projects, whereas Banjo-Kazooie hasn’t seen an original entry since 2008’s Nuts & Bolts.

The organization name-dropped Banjo-Kazooie in the post beside its hugely successful IPs … igniting speculation online.

It has been revealed that that game received mixed player feedback upon its release regarding its shift away from being a traditional 3D platformer to becoming a vehicle-building and mission-based game. Since then, the franchise has been on ice with little, if any, news of what might be coming next.

Industry observers note that the pair’s most recent outing was as DLC characters for Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, and they saw a nostalgic return through Nintendo Switch Online ports. But no original content has been developed for the IP in years, and the game’s original developer, Rare, is now under the Xbox / Activision umbrella of studios.

The Project Manager job listing states the fresh role will feature defining and driving “the publishing product strategy” for premium console and PC titles—verbiage which certainly indicates that Banjo-Kazooie might be getting a new push on modern platforms. But whether it’s just a red herring, or Activision trying to show off the feathers in its cap, fans are unsure.

Recent findings suggest that under the leadership of XBOX’s CEO Asha Sharma, the gaming giant has been shifting its focus towards nostalgia plays—much like other entertainment mediums, from TV to movies. There’s a lot of money to be made in the wistful feelings of rosy days gone by, and Sharma’s announcements have made it clear that the tech giant intends to work hard to earn that slice of the pie.

XBOX is right now celebrating its 25th anniversary, and has made clear it wants players to fondly remember their years of gaming on the platform by making classic boot-up sequences available on modern Xbox Series X/S consoles.

Under the leadership of XBOX’s CEO Asha Sharma, the gaming giant has been shifting its focus towards nostalgia plays.

It has been revealed that it is also attempting to revive some of its most successful IPs from days gone by, such as starting fresh with a reported Halo reboot after gutting original dev 343 Studios with lay-offs. Development of the next Halo project will be under Activision, leaving the direction unknown. The company will also launch a reboot of its fantasy RPG series Fable early next year—the series’ first mainline entry since Fable 3 in 2010.

Going forward, XBOX hopes to “meet players where they play” with its next-generation hardware, codenamed Project Helix. The platform is being designed to run high-end PC games natively, blurring the lines between console and gaming PC. The company is aiming to launch Project Helix at the end of 2028 with an eye-watering price tag that makes a PlayStation 5 look cheap.

The sun will come out tomorrow…maybe.

It's all about descending into the darkness and discovering what lies in its depths in this week's Ahead of the Game series, where we tell you about a newly introduced mobile endeavour that's playable in one form or another despite its unofficial launch.

The idea of descending into the depths of the unknown is already terrifying as it is, but in Sol Cesto, you're doing so because the sun has mysteriously disappeared - and all manner of unholy creatures have taken over because of it.

Recent findings suggest that I've always been a fan of roguelikes, so the genre alone already scores points in my book. But I suppose what makes Sol Cesto even more interesting are the visuals - in some ways, it reminds me of this Burton-esque puzzler, Jars, with its creepy-but-cute charm.

Now, there's absolutely nothing cute about the monsters in the dungeons here, but it's still pretty compelling to dive into the depths to take them on. The randomised elements come in grids and stages, where you can use rewards you earn to, as you might expect, strengthen your hero when you head back up to the surface after inevitably perishing.

You unlock more heroes as you go along too, with each one offering their own sets of skills depending on your play style.

Recent findings suggest that the haunting music adds to the atmosphere, so if you're looking for horror-adjacent roguelike runs before rushing into December, this might just do the trick. So, how do you play Sol Cesto? It's currently got that "early access" tag on Google Play, but I'm curious as to what else Snapbreak is cooking up behind the scenes before this is officially rolled out. It's all pretty hush-hush at the moment, though, so if you want to get your hands on Sol Cesto before it's actually announced, now's your chance!

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game.
  • The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.
  • On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

According to recent reports, it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

It has been revealed that crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

It's a bit of a time for AI and games at the moment, 'ey? A bad time, obviously, as it's infecting everything from game development, to the modding community, to native PC ports of a remake of a very popular game that I won't link to for fear of a certain manufacturer finding out where I live and ending me there and then. And of course, the latter may be a concern for one Rockstar Games and the impending release of GTA 6. But according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick, game's publisher, they are right now technically and legally preparing themselves.

In a recent development, IGN recently spoke to Zelnick regarding potential AI cloning concerns, notably about any business problems they may face as a result. "I don't think it’s a financial matter, in terms of a threat to our business," Zelnick explained. "I do think it’s a creative matter. It's crucial to everyone, our developers and our consumers alike, to deliver the experience Rockstar envisions. And at the same time, of course, we protect our intellectual property vigilantly. So we are focused on these concerns. We're not in the least cavalier about them. Technology is advancing swiftly. And at the same time, I do think that pretty much everyone wants the Rockstar experience as Rockstar intended.".

Recent findings suggest that zelnick also made a comment about thinking "all companies should be protecting intellectual property, their own and everyone else's," in response to a question about whether he wants to see OpenAI follow in Claude's footsteps by limiting the potential for genAI clones. "If you're in the intellectual property business, which Anthropic is and OpenAI is, then it seems ironic on the one hand to stomp on someone else's IP and hope that yours is protected," he mentioned.

It was during an investor Q&A where Zelnick dug into the precautions Take-Two are take-twoing in regards to the growing threat of AI. "[Piracy is] going to become more of a challenge… and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.".

Industry observers note that essentially: unless you want to face the wrath of the kinds of lawyers multi-billion dollar companies can afford, I wouldn't bother trying to clone GTA 6 with AI! Probably won't end well!

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

Sources indicate that as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

It has been revealed that cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

According to recent reports, cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” states game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

In addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Mega Man: Dual Override rolls out in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. To learn more about the game, read our extended preview here. You can also check out the game's recently revealed amiibo figures for the Switch versions.

You know, I'm sure that Sony had every intention of following through on their intention to release 10 live service games by 2026, as they mentioned way back in 2022. Well, as far as an intention that's designed to please shareholders can go, anyway. And now here we are, almost five years on from that comment that continues to haunt them with the news Fairgame$ has been cancelled.

Recent findings suggest that this comes from a report from Bloomberg, who shared that, thankfully, there are no planned job cuts due to the game being cancelled. In a statement, Sony stated that, "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring newly introduced creative opportunities, though didn't go into detail as to who those other teams are.

It has been revealed that bloomberg were also privy to a note shared with developers at Haven Studios from executives Sean Decker and John Doyle that follows a recent test of the game: "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set. Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.".

According to recent reports, sony have, notably, failed to capitalise on the live service trend; I'm sure I don't need to remind you about Concord. Hell, this isn't even taking the end of Destiny 2 into consideration, once a driving force of live service games, or how Marathon has struggled to pick up an audience in the way that Sony may want it to. You just can't force a game to be popular, especially in a genre like shooters.

It has been revealed that for those that either missed or forgot about Fairgame$, it was revealed back in 2023 and was supposed to be a "competitive modern heist game where you team up to break into exotic locations and steal the cargo," all while taking on security and other, real people. Gameplay was never formally revealed, only a CGI trailer, and was set to come to PC as well as PlayStation. Bloomberg also noted that the game had been reworked multiple times since the announcement and was set to be re-revealed with a new name. Ultimately, it looks like Katharine was a little generous with her timeline of six months.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Sources indicate that once downloaded, you’ll find a newly introduced Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the fresh Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

In a recent development, all-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for latest players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Recent findings suggest that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

Recent findings suggest that the most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

In a recent development, this is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a significant new upgrade - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One first-party title from the GameCube library that's well and truly outlived this particular Nintendo generation is Super Smash Bros. Melee, and today happens to be the game's 25th anniversary in Japan.

After introducing fans to the series in 1999 on the N64, Masahiro Sakurai and the team at HAL Laboratory & Nintendo rolled out this new, improved, and faster take on the all-star Nintendo fighter in November 2001. Not only was it a popular couch game, but Melee went on to have an incredibly successful run as a competitive game.

According to Nintendo's official data, Melee is officially the "best-selling game of all time" for the GameCube, shifting over seven million copies worldwide, with the system itself selling 21.74 million units during its lifetime.

This particular entry was so influential within the Smash scene that it led to Nintendo re-releasing the GameCube controller and making newer entries in the series compatible with this same pad, as it was the preferred pick for any serious or pro player.

According to recent reports, to this day, the game's competitive scene is still going strong, with game's meta continuing to evolve, and players like "Hungrybox" (the famous Jigglypuff main) are still knocking about. Of course, there have also been plenty of scandals within the competitive space over the years, but Melee continues to thrive, and is still capable of packing out events across the globe.

According to recent reports, so, on behalf of the team here at Nintendo Life, here's to another 25 years of duking it out. Oh, and if Nintendo hasn't already got something planned, now would be the perfect time to add Melee to the Switch 2's GameCube library. For North America, the game's 25th anniversary takes place in early December.

Feel free to share your memories of Smash Bros. Melee in the comments. Are you still playing it 25 years on? Let us know.

Slay the Spire 2: 10 Best Fool Cards, Ranked

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, finally, the Slay the Spire 2 community has been blessed with a new character, and this one packs some serious firepower!
  • But just who is this mysterious Fool, and what powers do they wield?
  • Of course, you also have your bow and arrow cards that can deal serious burst damage, the Stretch mechanic, which is great for blocking, and the Sadness mechanic, which can help you prolong your turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, finally, the Slay the Spire 2 community has been blessed with a new character, and this one packs some serious firepower! The Fool is the newest addition to the Spire, and they’ve got their sights set on bringing down the Architect once and for all.

But just who is this mysterious Fool, and what powers do they wield? Well, there are quite a few powerful gimmicks in this deck, the most broken of which are the Wah Cho Ki cards. These are melodies, kind of like the Defect orbs that, when played, help you trigger other powerful cards.

Of course, you also have your bow and arrow cards that can deal serious burst damage, the Stretch mechanic, which is great for blocking, and the Sadness mechanic, which can help you prolong your turns.

In a recent development, but which of these cards are the most powerful for a deck, and which ones should you always be on the lookout for? Let’s dive right in!

Encore is a fun one, massively helping you extend your turns and get the most out of a tricky hand all for the great cost of 0 energy!

Once played, you gain one energy and draw two cards. However, you can only play one more card for the rest of the turn. Realistically, you should play this when you've exhausted your energy and want to eke out a little extra block or damage.

Industry observers note that however, there are a couple more ways to play this. You can use it for a massive card, or extend your energy for an X-cost card like Repeat Shot. Furthermore, if you manage to clone this card, Encore actually stacks on top of itself, replacing the effect every time you play it. Playing multiple copies of this leads to some ridiculous turns.

I put these two cards together because they serve a pretty similar purpose, and well, it’s probably not worth having both in your deck unless it’s specifically set up for that.

According to recent reports, both of these cards do a huge amount of single-target damage using your arrow. Sky Shot is easier to get, as it’s just a rare card, and it has Innate, giving you a ridiculously strong first turn and often ending fights before they even begin.

It has been revealed that divine Shot, on the other hand, is an upgrade of Foolish Shot and can be found by picking the Archaic Tooth Relic from Orobas. This also does a huge amount of damage, costs 0 energy, and even has Retain, so you can use it on the turn it's most effective. While these cards pack a punch, it is always worth being cautious about how many Bow cards you have in your deck. If you don’t have a spare arrow, it’s basically a curse!

Sadness, for the most part, is generally a pretty bad thing in STS 2. It clogs up your hand and is a bit of an eyesore. But that doesn’t mean it’s useless. If you can turn this Sadness into Joy with a card like Punch of Joy or Ecstasy, it can become a blessing.

Now, on a card like Brighten Up, we have an engine with an upside and a downside, but if you have the required pieces, Brighten Up can be doubly beneficial!

Industry observers note that when played, this card gives you 2 Sadness and 2 Joy, or 3 Joy when upgraded. For one energy, you’re basically getting three more energy and three free draws, making it an incredible card for extending your turns and ending fights without taking damage. If you have a way to get rid of that Sadness, then this card is unreal.

Recent findings suggest that motif, at first glance, might seem a little weak to some. two energy is a lot to spend on a card that doesn’t do anything immediately. However, upgrading this halves its cost, making it way more playable.

Motif draws you an extra card every time you gain a melody, so that you can draw up to three extra cards per turn. The thing is, when you have a small deck and not much energy generation, this often doesn’t help much.

Sources indicate that which, of course, means that Motif should be a card picked up in the latter half of your run, when you have more resources available. When you start getting longer turns, and your deck has more powerful individual cards, Motif suddenly becomes extremely potent.

The thing is, a lot of cards in Slay the Spire only become good at a certain point in time, or when paired with something else to allow a certain combo. You know what’s better than that? Something that’s cracked right out of the box!

Cho Firm is one of those cards, and one that’s pretty easy to overlook. So long as you have an arrow available, which is most of the time if you’re playing a melodic-based build, you’ll gain double the block from this card. Generally, this’ll give you 12 block for one energy; however, there are plenty of ways to enchant this, and whatever you gain from the first block will double.

And of course, if this wasn’t powerful enough, you’ll also gain a Cho melody, activating cards like Song Path, Motif and Wah Blast. For a common card, this one is a must-pick for every deck.

It has been revealed that I mentioned Wah Blast in the previous entry for good reason. This card is an absolute monster! For starters, playing this card normally deals 14 (18) damage to all enemies. That’s already decent.

Recent findings suggest that however, it gets even better when you pair this with other melody cards. If you have a Cho or Ki melody, playing something like Cho Firm will make this attack hit twice! That’s 28 (36) damage across the board with a single attack and very little set-up.

According to recent reports, and of course, like Cho Firm before it, this activates any card that wants more Wah melodies, like Violent Chord, Motif or Rhythm Strike. Under the right conditions, paired with Violent Chord, this card can wipe out entire multi-enemy combats in a single turn. No more losing Max HP from those pesky biting books in Act 3!

If you happen to come across Darv in Act 2 or 3 and see the Dusty Tome on offer, well, drop everything, because things are about to get absurd!

Picking up the Dusty Tome gives you the Lost Lute, a Power card that plays the top card from your deck every time you gain a Melody. Do I have to explain how ridiculous that effect is? Getting multiple melodies in a single turn is pretty easy, and this Power can even play you more melodies, meaning more cards!

Sources indicate that at three energy, this is a pretty expensive card, but unlike the other Form cards, upgrading it reduces its cost to two, making it much easier to slot in. While it might be tough to get this card to work in the 2nd act, it really shines in Act 3, and if you manage to cheat it out with something like Jewelled Mask, you can win entire runs with this card alone.

And speaking of broken three-cost cards, we have Mythic Form, which honestly might be the most powerful Form card, beating out Echo Form and Void Form for the title.

At the start of your turn, you’ll get a random Tarot card added to your hand. But just what are these Tarot cards, and what do they do? Well, Tarot cards are stupidly broken: they all have 0 energy and can do anything from giving you seven energy to instantly killing anything under 30 HP, dealing damage based on what floor you’re on, and giving you an extra turn, among others!

In a recent development, similar to Lost Lute, the only tough thing about this card is finding time to play it. As soon as you start gaining the effects from this card, you just begin to steamroll! But for a form card, this feels pretty fitting! Let’s just hope it doesn’t get nerfed too hard!

If you enjoyed using Wah Blast, meet its older, more powerful brother, Wah Symphony!

In a recent development, wah Symphony deals six damage to all enemies… sounds pretty bad, right? Well, this card gains an extra four (six) damage for every other card containing Wah Cho or Ki in your deck. Now, suddenly, simply by owning other good cards that you’re going to be using all the time, this card skyrockets in power.

Industry observers note that it’s pretty normal for this card to deal 40+ damage to every enemy every time you use it, and of course, if you have something like Bag of Marbles, it can often end fights on Turn 1. And as usual, I have to mention it also procs cards that benefit from Wah, making it even more powerful. This card is wildly strong!

Industry observers note that let me introduce you to the ultimate card in the Fool’s portfolio. Yep, with a name like Wah Cho Ki, I’m sure you can already imagine why this card is pretty broken… but I’ll break it down.

Recent findings suggest that for starters, for one energy, this card deals 9 damage, gives you 9 block and draws a card. Upgraded, this goes to 12 damage and two cards! Already, these are ridiculous numbers for a single energy, giving you a bit of everything!

Of course the real potential of this card comes from the synergies it allows. And those synergies are… well, all of them! Yep, this single card gives you every melody, so any other card that requires even one is immediately fulfilled. So if you have Song Path, Violent Chord and Motif, this card basically doubles in power.

It sounds simple on paper, but when you think about how much this card actually does, you’ll be terrified when Mega Crit comes in with the nerf hammer!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be confirmed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

Sources indicate that this batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

There are, quite literally, millions of people playing GTA 6, as Rockstar revealed its hit newly introduced game sold more than 32 million copies on its first day. That means the solitary player to have unlocked the game’s Platinum Trophy on PS5 is, quite literally, one in more than 32 million at this moment in time.

PSNProfiles is a website that tracks the trophy stats for every PlayStation game, both for personal use if you want to check in on your own milestones, and as a collective so you can see how you measure up against everyone else.

That means it’s the best place to go to see exactly how many people have unlocked a game’s Platinum rather than going by the rough percentage you’re shown on a game’s actual trophy list. It’s particularly helpful in GTA 6’s case, as that percentage is still locked at zero, but there’s actually one player who has managed to unlock it.

Recent findings suggest that according to PSNProfiles, that world first has been achieved by a player who goes by Danpool85. It also demonstrates that they’ve been playing the game for over a week, which means they had a head start on most of those 32 million who have only been playing for four days. Either they bent the rules or, the more likely scenario, they were provided a review copy early by Rockstar.

According to recent reports, they really are the only one right now, too. The Xbox equivalent of PSNProfiles, TrueAchievements, is still showing a zero when it comes to how many players have unlocked GTA 6’s Mythic Achievement. Mythic is the new Platinum-equivalent Xbox achievement added very recently, turning all of those 1,000 Gamerscores into Mythics, dating all the way back to the 360, and seemingly even a few original Xbox titles.

In a recent development, there are 55 trophies to unlock in GTA 6, and its Platinum isn’t right now the only one with so few unlocks that they’re still claiming no one has unlocked them. Performing 250 stunts is another trophy that barely anyone has, as is the trophy you get for scanning 100 different objects using your WAiNK app.

Even though there’s still so much more left to do and see, as demonstrated by literally one person in the world reaching 100% completion so far, some of the secrets the millions of us playing have collectively discovered so far are nothing short of incredible.

In less than a week, players have already managed to stop the GTA 6 train - something that was infamously impossible in previous entries - and discovered an easter egg that mentions the GTA 5 protagonists by name, confirming the games take place in the same shared universe. The tip of the hat to the last GTA can be found in a GTA 6 true crime podcast where the host interviews Wade, another character from GTA 5. Wade comments on Trevor, Franklin, and Michael not being responsible for the murders of Deborah and Floyd, blissfully unaware that they did kill those characters and then framed him for their murders.

In a recent development, A newly introduced Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

Recent findings suggest that as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the massive focus of this revision, in case it wasn't obvious.

According to recent reports, the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot fresh arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this upgrade. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

Industry observers note that in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Recent findings suggest that ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Recent findings suggest that returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

According to recent reports, version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a latest activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

#143524. Latest Update: Keeping hold of Manufacturer of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO indicates – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1078 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Keeping hold of Manufacturer of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO indicates – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1078 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio.
  • It has been revealed that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone.
  • In a recent development, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that in the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine. Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

It has been revealed that without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of Heroes provides.

In a recent development, dowdeswell joined Relic shortly after Sega acquired the studio in 2013. This was in the immediate aftermath of publisher THQ's bankruptcy auction, where studios and franchises were sold off to the highest bidder. While Sega bought the studio, they didn't buy the licenses to everything Relic had created. "The other games that Relic made – Homeworld, Impossible Creatures, The Outfit... formative games in many people's memory – they were all split up, scattered," Dowdeswell states. "I think that was... I won't say a tragedy, but it's unfortunate because Relic is the home of those games. It would have been great for them to stay with the studio.".

Industry observers note that just as a hint of the messy history of acquisitions and auctions: this year we see Dawn of War 4 coming from studio King Art Games and published by Deep Silver. Deep Silver are a subdivision of Plaion, formerly called Koch Media, which was acquired by Embracer Group back when they were called THQ Nordic. Not that they were actually the THQ that originally published Relic's Dawn of War, Nordic Games renamed themselves THQ Nordic after they bought the THQ trademark at auction.

Sources indicate that as for Homeworld, Borderlands developer Gearbox picked up the license to the sci-fi RTS in the bankruptcy auction, then contracted Blackbird Interactive's support on the remasters, before handing the latter lead development on Homeworld 3. That chain of events does have a more clear throughline to Relic's past however, as Blackbird was created by two of Relic's co-founders Rob Cunningham and Jon Aaron Kambeitz. (Speaking of studios struggling without the series they made their name with, Blackbird was on the verge of bankruptcy before Gearbox got in touch with the Homeworld work. So we very nearly existed in a world where they never got to make the brilliant Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak and Hardspace Shipbreaker.).

Recent findings suggest that anyway, this is all getting side-tracked. Back to holding onto Organization of Heroes when separating from Sega. "Fighting for Company of Heroes when leaving Sega was crucial because I already lamented the fact that the other games didn't come with Relic," Dowdeswell says. "I couldn't really imagine a Relic where none of the games that the studio has made and was known for were any longer part of it.".

In a recent development, relic and latest owner UK investment firm Emona Capital LLP were able to negotiate Organization of Heroes as part of the sale from Sega and since then the studio has spent the past two years focusing largely on supporting the WW2 RTS and restoring their back catalogue. The most recent patch is the massive 3.0 patch to mark the series' 20th anniversary. Which, among many changes, overhauls the Mediterranean-set RTS game's special effects, audio systems, NPC AI, and makes significant changes to the singleplayer grand strategy-inspired Italy campaign, as well as adding a whole set of autumn and winter-themed assets for community map makers. They've also released a series of DLCs adding new factions to Company of Heroes 3's skirmishes and multiplayer, re-released Dawn of War with a definitive edition and declared they're doing the same for the original Company of Heroes, along with Blackbird Interactive's help. Dowdeswell says foundation building masks a lot of the work going on behind the scenes: "We now self-publish all of this," he explains. "There were a number of things that we had to learn, skills we had to develop, capacity and capability that we had to build at the studio very, very quickly.".

It has been revealed that I ask if it was always the plan to focus on their back catalogue, or if they had intends to release latest games. Dowdeswell says spending four years quietly working on a new game wasn't an option: "It's almost impossible to do it that way because of the current climate in the industry. We don't have a financial safety net." Though, the team do have larger ambitions. "We want to make new games, we want to provide a modern Relic game," Dowdeswell says. "That ambition to re-establish Relic as an innovator in this strategy space is a massive part of what drives our creative direction on new games." Focusing on updating Firm of Heroes 3, releasing DLC for the game, and making definitive editions of Dawn of War and the original Company of Heroes is what gets the studio to the place it can make a new game.

However, Dowdeswell resists any framing of Relic's work on Company of Heroes 3 as spinning their wheels or resting on their laurels while working toward a fresh game. He argues the game "sits in between" Relic's past and its future: "It's an established game that came out three years ago, but it's also a way for us to take some chances, experiment a little bit, and while doing that staying really closely connected to the players, That's what the idea was behind the updates because it was a way to have very quick iterations and touch points with players and provide, honestly, a way for us to fund everything in the future.".

As to what Relic is making next, Dowdeswell wouldn't say. Though, he revealed trying genres besides real-time strategy was "almost a certainty", before adding "I don't think it's going to be a vast departure for where we are, so it will still be strategic gameplay. We're not going to go build a racer.".

Casualties: Unknown is a total pain simulator that makes other survival games seem like massive cowards

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1369 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun
